applicationPool.reason: a real SwiftUI application: import SwiftUI and struct types conforming to View throughout damus/Features and damus/Shared. It ships a damusUITests XCUITest target, and onboarding, key generation, login by nsec, settings and the post composer are all local, with relays affecting only feed content. Upstream CI at HEAD builds for an iOS Simulator destination with no signing step, which is direct evidence the simulator build needs no identity
applicationPool.candidateDefectsBasis: three pairs verified, four more examined and rejected

applicationPool.reason: SwiftUI screens under iOS/New/Views with no login and no onboarding gate; the tab bar loads immediately, and Settings, Backups and the built-in local files source are fully offline. The entitlements file requests push, iCloud and CloudKit only, with no application groups, so blanking DEVELOPMENT_TEAM is enough for an unsigned simulator build

pure SwiftUI, but without an account only two tabs render, timeline and settings, and timeline needs the network, so only the settings surface is reachable offline. The build additionally needs a synthesized IceCubesApp.xcconfig because the real file is gitignored and only a template is committed, and there is no UI test target to inherit

a genuine SwiftUI application with struct YatteeApp: App and WindowGroup, no onboarding gate, and the whole settings tree plus home customization reachable with zero configured instances. Containment: DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = 78Z5H3M6RJ is hardcoded eight times in the project file and SPM pulls MPVKit binary xcframeworks, so the build is not hermetic. No UI test target. Its best defect has no issue and no pull request, only a commit message, so nothing is selected from it

SwiftUI dominant by file count, 426 files importing SwiftUI against 109 importing UIKit, but the application shell is UIKit: AppDelegate is a UIResponder with a SceneDelegate, and the only struct conforming to App is the watchOS one, so the SwiftUI scene lifecycle this target claims is not what drives the app. The full application target also carries push, associated domains, the autofill credential provider, iCloud, application groups, keychain sharing and NFC, and the build path requires XcodeGen, SwiftGen, SwiftLint and Sourcery through mint with a pinned Xcode. The entitlement-free BitwardenKit framework is a viable containment island. Defect linkage is by Jira ticket key rather than a closing reference, which makes pairs expensive to derive
applicationPool.candidateDefectsBasis: six issue key matches, four pairs proven

applicationPool.reason: genuine SwiftUI over the Composable Architecture, and solo play is fully local with server and Game Center failures deliberately swallowed, so no account is needed. Two containment costs: the license is a custom NOASSERTION file that must be read before use, and the clone currently fails Git LFS smudge because the repository exceeded its LFS budget, with 175 image and audio assets tracked by LFS, so the working tree can only be materialized with GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE and substitute assets

the Pulse Demo iOS target in Demo/Pulse.xcodeproj is real SwiftUI with struct PulseDemo_iOS: App and WindowGroup, is fully offline against a mock log store, and has no entitlements file at all, which is the cleanest signing story in the pool. It is held back because almost every fix is library-layer and the SwiftUI view fixes carry no linked issue

not SwiftUI at the candidate revisions: 228 files import SwiftUI against 284 importing UIKit plus 441 Objective-C files, and there is no struct conforming to App and no WindowGroup anywhere; the entry point is a UIResponder AppDelegate. GitHub issues are disabled and tracking is Phabricator, so no pair can ever be issue-linked here

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the strongest candidate for this target. The fix ships its own XCUITest, testPostComposerCursorPosition, whose oracle is a hard string equality on the text view value rather than a layout heuristic, and the defect is SwiftUI state-driven text binding flowing through a UIViewRepresentable, which is exactly the SwiftUI view identity and update path the adapter observes through XCUITest
selectedDefects.caveat: the accessibility identifiers post_button and post_composer_text_view were introduced by the fix, so the harness must port them onto the affected build for the driver to address the same elements. The damusUITests target itself already exists at the affected revision
remaining: build both revisions for the simulator with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO and DEVELOPMENT_TEAM blanked, and record the exact command and result
port the two accessibility identifiers onto the affected build and record that as an instrumentation delta, not a behavior change
state the exact identity and authority for the observable, and minimize the trigger
run three affected reproductions and three fixed controls on a reset simulator with reset evidence
record neighboring legal behavior: typing into a different text field must keep the caret in place on the affected build

no candidate has been built. Every simulatorBuildWithoutSigning entry is an inspection of project settings and the entitlements file at the affected revision, not an executed xcodebuild, so buildQualified is null for the whole pool

the six candidates come from four applications, but the two strongest are both damus, and the Aidoku settings freeze candidate is at risk of being dropped because the fix lands in a UITabBarController subclass rather than in a SwiftUI View. If both the Aidoku freeze and the isowords candidate are dropped, the target falls to four

the largest and most rigorously maintained iOS codebases in this space are not SwiftUI-driven at their candidate revisions. wikipedia-ios, firefox-ios, Signal-iOS and KeePassium were each rejected on a per-revision framework check, and wikipedia-ios additionally has GitHub issues disabled, so no issue-linked pair can ever be derived there. The qualifying pool is therefore small independent applications, which is the structural reason this target's inventory is thin
